rubrics.criterion: In the geofire-common algorithm source, the internal seams that carry one position (validation of the coordinate values, geohash encoding, bounding-box geometry, distance computation) each accept the position as one grouped location value; no such seam still takes one position as separate latitude/longitude scalar parameters, and genuinely independent neighbors (radius, precision, bit count, geohash) remain ordinary separate parameters.
rubrics.rationale: The coordinate-owning helpers of the algorithms package are the primary spread of the split-pair threading in this task; each of these seams currently consumes the two numbers of one point as unrelated scalars while the surrounding code is built around tuple-valued locations.

rubrics.criterion: Grouping preserves location identity: every internal grouped value treated as a location carries [latitude, longitude] in that order (a value reaching one of these seams is never transposed at the boundary), the geohash produced for a given point is unchanged (the bit interleave still applies the slots in the algorithm's order without re-reversing the pair inside the grouped value), and where two positions meet (distance between a tracked point and the query center, or between two locations) they travel as two separate grouped values whose slots are correctly paired - not as one flattened multi-number container and not with the two positions' numbers interchanged.
rubrics.rationale: This task's split seams include a reversed-slot-order kernel and a two-location computation; a repair that merely hides the two numbers inside a different container, or that pairs a latitude with the wrong longitude, produces self-consistent code that no test failure exposes, so identity and pairing are graded explicitly.

rubrics.criterion: GeoQuery holds the query center as one grouped center value rather than as two sibling scalar fields, and the center's consumers (the geohash-bounds recomputation, the public center() getter, criteria updates, and per-key distance measurements against the center) use that one value directly instead of recombining two separate number members at each boundary.
rubrics.rationale: The query engine's center state is the state manifestation of this task; center-derived consumers (bounds, comparisons, the public getter) currently rebuild an array from two fields on every use.

rubrics.criterion: Incoming realtime locations reach the GeoQuery recording/tracking logic as one grouped value on the child-added and child-changed paths: the decoded snapshot location is not split into two scalars that are then passed as separate arguments into the engine's location-update seam, and that recording path stores, compares and dispatches the position as one value.
rubrics.rationale: The realtime ingestion path (child added/child changed into the tracked-state update, including the in/out-of-query comparisons and callback dispatch) is where the split is most deeply threaded; it is also the path a shallow repair is most likely to leave untouched.

rubrics.criterion: On the write path, GeoFire.set passes the validated location to the storage codec as one grouped value, and the storage codec encodes the stored document ({'.priority', 'g', 'l'} with the location field) from that one value without taking the position as separate latitude/longitude parameters beside the derived geohash.
rubrics.rationale: The codec seam plus the GeoFire.set caller threading form the persistence-side portion of this task; the codec currently re-pairs two separate scalar parameters twice (validation and stored field) while the persisted shape must stay identical.

rubrics.criterion: During criteria updates, the per-key distance recomputation iterates the tracked locations and measures each tracked position and the new center as grouped values (the tracked record's stored location remains a single grouped value), without destructuring a tracked location into scalar locals only to pass them as separate arguments to a distance seam.
rubrics.rationale: The criteria-update loop is a distinct execution path of the same relation: it currently splits each tracked record's location to feed a scalar distance helper, so the regrouping must also hold on this path.

rubrics.criterion: The key-removal path (the exited-key distance computation performed when a location is removed, using the last known position) computes its distance from one grouped position and the grouped center value, without taking the removed location apart into two scalars for a helper.
rubrics.rationale: Removal is a small side branch of the same relationship; a repair that regroups the added/changed paths but leaves the removal branch splitting the position would leak the old shape on a rarely traveled path.

rubrics.criterion: A seam remains whose only purpose is carrying the split coordinate parts of one position: an internal helper, wrapper or pair of number fields that accepts or persists bare latitude/longitude values for one point and merely repacks them for the grouped code around it (for example a residual forwarding helper taking two coordinate scalars to call a value-oriented function, or two kept number fields mirroring the center).
rubrics.rationale: Partial repairs in this codebase often leave an adapter that converts the new grouped calling convention back into the old two-number shape for one or two owners; such repacking seams recreate the exact relationship the task removes.

rubrics.criterion: The split survives under new names or shapes: positions are still handed around as two scalar parameters (or two primitive number fields) with merely renamed or vocabulary-free names (e.g. a/b, first/second, x/y), or a grouped value is immediately re-split into two scalars at the next seam where the pair is again treated as unrelated numbers.
rubrics.rationale: The cheapest textual dodge for this task keeps two parameters per position and renames them; that change repairs nothing, so its presence must count against cleanup.

rubrics.criterion: An observable contract is altered: a public API signature or the exported symbol set of either package changed, the GeoQuery callback contract (key, location, distanceFromCenter with null position/distance where appropriate) or the ready/entered/exited/moved event behavior changed, or the stored Firebase document shape for a location changed.
rubrics.rationale: The whole repair happens behind a published API and a persisted data format; these are the surfaces a coordinate-pipeline refactor must not disturb.

rubrics.criterion: Partial criteria updates regress: a radius-only (or center-only) update on a query whose center sits at latitude 0 no longer keeps/moves the center exactly as before, extraneous criteria attributes are no longer rejected, or a tracked key is lost (or its in/out-of-query status recomputed wrongly) when the query recomputes for new criteria.
rubrics.rationale: The criteria-update seam is where a regrouped value is easiest to corrupt silently, because the keep-it behavior depends on falsy values (latitude 0) rather than truthiness; the suite covers it only on specific paths.

rubrics.criterion: Validation behavior or diagnostics changed: some non-array, wrong-length, non-number, NaN or out-of-range input is no longer rejected the same way, the error message text for an invalid location changed (including how the offending pair is rendered inside the message), or the checks run in a different order in either package.
rubrics.rationale: The validation seam is one of the regrouped callables and formats the offending pair directly into its error text; a repair that changes the rendering, reorders the checks, or drops coordinate-value checks changes observable behavior.
